title: Light
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Light Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: Recall and use the laws of reflection and describe the image in a plane mirror; describe refraction and recall and apply refractive index n = sin i ÷ sin r and n = speed of light in a vacuum ÷ speed of light in the medium; define critical angle, recall and apply sin c = 1 ÷ n and describe total internal reflection and its use in optical fibres; describe the action of a thin converging lens, define focal length and principal focus, draw ray diagrams and state the nature of the image formed for different object distances, including uses such as a magnifying glass, camera and projector (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on light: reflection, plane mirrors, refraction, refractive index, critical angle, total internal reflection, optical fibres and converging lenses. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: n = sin i ÷ sin r = c ÷ v
key_sub: sin c = 1 ÷ n; angles are measured from the normal.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light reflects with equal angles and refracts when its speed changes.

  • Reflection: i = r, measured from the normal. A plane mirror gives a virtual, upright, same-size, laterally inverted image.
  • Refraction: n = sin i ÷ sin r = c ÷ v. Light bends towards the normal entering a denser medium.
  • Total internal reflection: from denser to less dense medium, with i greater than the critical angle c, where sin c = 1 ÷ n.
  • Converging lens: object beyond 2F gives a real, diminished image (camera); between F and 2F gives a real, magnified image (projector); inside F gives a virtual, magnified image (magnifying glass).
Example

i = 40°, r = 25°. n?

n = sin 40° ÷ sin 25° = 0.643 ÷ 0.423

Answer: 1.52

Example

n = 1.5. Critical angle?

sin c = 1 ÷ 1.5 = 0.667

Answer: 41.8°

Common mistakes

  • Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal.
  • Writing n = sin r ÷ sin i (the answer becomes less than 1).
  • Saying total internal reflection happens when light goes from air into glass.
  • Thinking a converging lens always forms a real image.

faq.q: How do you calculate refractive index?
faq.a: Use n = sin i ÷ sin r for light entering the medium from air, or n = c ÷ v using the speeds of light.

faq.q: When does total internal reflection happen?
faq.a: When light travels from a denser medium towards a less dense one and the angle of incidence is larger than the critical angle.

faq.q: What image does a magnifying glass form?
faq.a: When the object is closer than the principal focus, a converging lens forms a virtual, upright, magnified image on the same side as the object.

items.q: What two conditions are needed for total internal reflection?
c: The surface must be a mirror.
The angle of incidence must be zero.
Light must travel from a denser to a less dense medium, and the angle of incidence must be greater than the critical angle.
Light must go from air into glass at any angle.
items.e: Used in optical fibres.

items.q: A ray of light hits a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of 40°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection (both measured from the normal).

items.q: Describe the image in a plane mirror.
c: virtual, upright, the same size and laterally inverted, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front
items.e: It cannot be formed on a screen.

items.q: What is the focal length of a lens?
c: the distance from the object to the image
the distance between the optical centre of the lens and the principal focus
items.e: A thicker converging lens has a shorter focal length.

items.q: The angle of incidence on a plane mirror is 20°. What is the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray?
items.e: The angle between them is i + r = 20° + 20° = 40°.

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the normal is 25°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 25° (both measured from the normal).

items.q: The angle of incidence is 25°. What is the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray?
items.e: Each ray makes 25° with the normal, so together 50°.

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 65° to the mirror surface. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of incidence = 90° − 65° = 25° (from the normal), so the angle of reflection is 25°.

items.q: When light enters glass from air at an angle, which way does it bend?
items.e: It slows down.

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 75° to the mirror surface. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of incidence = 90° − 75° = 15° (from the normal), so the angle of reflection is 15°.

items.q: Xin Yi stands 2.5 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is the image behind the mirror?
items.e: The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the normal is 50°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 50° (both measured from the normal).

items.q: Ahmad stands 1.5 m from a plane mirror and walks 1 m towards it. How far is he now from his image?
items.e: New distance from mirror = 0.5 m; image distance = 0.5 m; separation = 1 m.

items.q: What is the critical angle?
c: the angle of refraction in glass
the angle at which light reflects from a mirror
the largest possible angle of incidence
the angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction is 90°
items.e: sin c = 1 ÷ n.

items.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the normal is 20°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 20° (both measured from the normal).

items.q: What is refraction?
c: the splitting of light into colours only
the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another because its speed changes
the bouncing of light off a surface
items.e: Light slows down in glass.

items.q: Hafiz stands 0.5 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is he from the image?
items.e: Image distance = 0.5 m behind, so separation = 0.5 + 0.5 = 1 m.

items.q: The angle of incidence is 65°. What is the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray?
items.e: Each ray makes 65° with the normal, so together 130°.

items.q: Mei Ling stands 3 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is the image behind the mirror?
items.e: The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

items.q: Jun Jie stands 1.5 m from a plane mirror and walks 0.5 m towards it. How far is he now from his image?
items.e: New distance from mirror = 1 m; image distance = 1 m; separation = 2 m.

items.q: A ray enters perspex (refractive index 1.5) from air and is refracted at 25° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1.5 × sin 25°, so i = 39.3°.

items.q: A ray hits the inside of a glass block (critical angle 42°) at 30° to the normal. What happens?
c: Most of the light is refracted out into the air.
It is refracted towards the normal.
items.e: 30° is less than 42°.

items.q: A ray of light enters a block from air with an angle of incidence of 35° and an angle of refraction of 22°. What is the refractive index?
items.e: n = sin i ÷ sin r = sin 35° ÷ sin 22° = 1.53.

items.q: What is the principal focus (F) of a converging lens?
c: the point where rays parallel to the principal axis meet after passing through the lens
the point where the image is always formed
items.e: Its distance from the lens is the focal length.

items.q: Light passes from air into crown glass (refractive index 1.52) at an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of refraction?
Light passes from air into crown glass (refractive index 1.52) at an angle of incidence of 55°. What is the angle of refraction?
The refractive index of crown glass is 1.52. What is the speed of light in crown glass? (speed of light in air = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
The refractive index of perspex is 1.5. What is the speed of light in perspex? (speed of light in air = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
Light passes from air into crown glass (refractive index 1.52) at an angle of incidence of 50°. What is the angle of refraction?
Why does a swimming pool look shallower than it really is?
c: Light bends towards the normal leaving water.
Light from the bottom bends away from the normal as it leaves the water, so the bottom appears higher.
items.e: This is apparent depth.

items.q: Light passes from air into diamond (refractive index 2.42) at an angle of incidence of 25°. What is the angle of refraction?
Why are optical fibres used for internet cables in Singapore?
c: They carry large amounts of data as light pulses with little loss and no electrical interference.
items.e: Also used in endoscopes.

items.q: Light travels at 2.25 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s in a material. What is its refractive index? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
When light leaves glass into air at an angle, which way does it bend?
items.e: It speeds up.

items.q: The refractive index of water is 1.33. What is the speed of light in water? (speed of light in air = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
State the laws of reflection.
c: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.
The angle of incidence is twice the angle of reflection.
Only the angles of rough surfaces are equal.
items.e: Angles are measured from the normal.

items.q: A ray enters a glass block along the normal (angle of incidence 0°). What happens?
c: It passes straight through without bending, though it slows down.
items.e: No change in direction.

items.q: Why do prisms in binoculars use total internal reflection instead of mirrors?
c: Total internal reflection reflects almost all the light, so the image is brighter.
items.e: No silvering to wear away.

items.q: A ray enters water (refractive index 1.33) from air and is refracted at 20° to the normal. What was the angle of incidence?
items.e: sin i = n × sin r = 1.33 × sin 20°, so i = 27.1°.

items.q: Light travels at 1.97 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s in a material. What is its refractive index? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)

items.q: Why do the letters AMBULANCE appear reversed on the front of an ambulance?
c: Drivers see them the right way round in their rear-view mirror because a plane mirror gives lateral inversion.
So that pedestrians can read it easily.
items.e: Left and right are swapped in a mirror image.

c: Most of it is refracted out into the air, bending away from the normal.
It passes straight through without bending.
items.e: Total internal reflection happens only when light goes from a denser medium to a less dense one and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.
